findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed two sanitizer buckets measure 0ppm quaternary ammonia during today’s visit. The PIC was informed and the bucket was replaced, measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia with a test strip. Inspector recommends increasing the frequency of bucket replacement. Printed labels are used to indicate the discard time for sanitizer, but the bucket measuring 0ppm was not due to expire for another two hours.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the green shelves holding pizza dough and rolling cart holding raw chicken to be soiled with microbial growth. The PIC was informed and plans to deep clean/sanitize the shelving. Ensure staff are monitoring cleanliness in the cooler and sanitizing surfaces frequently to prevent the accumulation of microbial growth. Ensure the shelves are clean to sight and touch prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the bottom shelf of the stainless steel table across from the chicken fryers to be rusted and in disrepair. This shelf is used to store extra broaster equipment, which comes in direct contact with food. Ensure this table is sealed or replaced prior to the next routine inspection.

Inspector also observed the green wire shelves in the dish area to be rusted and in disrepair. These shelves hold clean dishes, which are direct food contact surfaces. Ensure these shelves are sealed or replaced prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the dish machine measure a maximum temperature of 150.8F after multiple repeated attempts. The PIC discovered that the booster was not functioning properly. The PIC contacted support and fixed the machine. The machine then measured 161F with the dish puck. Ensure staff are monitoring the machine to prevent future violations.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
The inspector observed the following time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods to be held past their 7-day date mark:
1. Cauliflower (discard date 1/8/26)
2. Alfredo sauce (discard date 1/6/26)
3. Ranch dressing (discard date 16/2026)

The PIC was informed and these items were voluntarily discarded. Ensure staff are checking date marks at the beginning and end of each day to prevent the use of expired items.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee don a new pair of gloves without handwashing. Education was conducted regarding proper hand washing. Ensure staff are hand washing before donning a new pair of gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed triple sink to measure 0ppm quaternary ammonia. The PIC immediately recognized that the Quat-San bucket under the triple sink was not properly connected; the tubing was not far enough into the sanitizer bucket. The triple sink was drained and refilled, with a quaternary ammonia concentration of 200ppm. The violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.comment: Observed dish machine in use following violation #16 from the inspection conducted on 3/6/25 being unresolved. The dish machine was out of temperature and inadequate for sanitization. It seems there is a lack of communication between the Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) and the rest of the staff regarding necessary repairs and change of procedure. Ensure the dish staff is informed at all times regarding proper dish handling and sanitization as well as any changes to procedure. A spot check will be conducted on 3/17/2025 along with the follow-up on the dish machine to ensure proper communication between CFPM’s and staff.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(L) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (L) EMPLOYEES are properly SANITIZING cleaned multiuse EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS before they are reused, through routine monitoring of solution temperature and exposure time for hot water SANITIZING, and chemical concentration, pH, temperature, and exposure time for chemical SANITIZING.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed dish machine in use following violation #16 from the inspection conducted on 3/6/25 being unresolved. The dish machine was out of temperature and inadequate for sanitization. The PIC confirmed that the dish machine has not been serviced since the previous inspection, and there was no sanitizer in the triple sink. Since the dish machine is still not reaching the minimum temperature for sanitization (165F), it cannot be used to sanitize dishes or equipment. A triple sink with sanitizer was prepared during the inspection. Ensure staff are using the triple sink until the repairs are complete. The original follow-up date for the dish machine, 3/17/2025, still applies.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed heat-sanitizing dish machine to temp 157F after 5 passes with the dish puck. PIC was informed of the issue, and maintenance happened to be on site for  another repair. Dish staff prepared a triple sink, and the sanitizer was tested at 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure staff are using triple sink to sanitize until dish machine is repaired. A follow-up is scheduled for 3/17/2025 to ensure the dish machine is in working order with a temperature greater than 165F.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed 8 containers of cut vegetables in the salad bar cooler and 4 containers of cut vegetables on the salad bar itself to have date marking indicating the food items were past their acceptable serving date. PIC was informed that the containers were out of date, and all 12 containers were voluntarily discarded. Ensure staff are checking date marks on produce containers at the start and end of each day and discarding away out-of-date items. Violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: Observed floor drain in dish room to be overflowing. Dish machine is routed to floor drain, and drain overflows upon use of machine. PIC was informed of overflowing drain and plans to have a plumber inspect the drain. PIC stated that this issue is ongoing and has been using a drain snake “when the room floods.” A follow-up is scheduled for 3/10/2025 to ensure drain is operating properly.
findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed box of chicken breading to not be covered and protected from airborne contamination. Cover box of breading to avoid airborne contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Observed CFPM on duty to not have allergen awareness training certification. Provide allergen awareness training certification for all CFPM.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.comment:

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.
